newsitem.title: USA: US debt portfolios hardly changed Oct 15 wk-survey.
newsitem.headline: US debt portfolios hardly changed Oct 15 wk-survey.

text.p: Offsetting investment maneuvers by U.S. money managers left debt portfolios little changed on average, according to a survey by Stone & McCarthy Research Associates Inc.

"There was little change in portfolio structural statistics in the latest survey," the report said. "There were good flows in both directions, and movement in both directions along the (yield) curve."

In the week ended October 15, the survey's bear/bull index arithmetic reading rose to 4.44 from 4.16 the previous week, while the asset-weighted number rebounded to 4.33, up from 4.03 in the previous period, according the report.
A number above 5.00 is seen as indicating investors are mostly long on the market.
The cash/assets ratio fell to 6.98 percent from 7.08 percent.
Duration bogey held mostly steady at 4.05 on an arithmetic basis and 4.67 on a weighted basis.
Duration bogey is the level of asset or liability duration sought in the management of a portfolio.
Duration refers to a portfolio's average maturity and is used by portfolio managers to calculate exposure to risk.

Twenty-four percent of the portfolio managers polled said they were planning to be active in the coming week, unchanged from the week before. The bear/bull index collected among those intending to be active was 4.83, down from 4.17 the previous week.
The Stone & McCarthy survey is conducted by the research firm weekly. It includes 25 market participants with total assets of about $100 billion, the firm said.
* Table provided by Stone and McCarthy Research Associates.
** Respondents intending to adjust portfolio in coming week.
